title: When your mind goes blank and the answer comes out generic
subtitle: Why it happens, what to ask yourself on the day, and how to dig out the detail at home so it is there when you need it.

points.head: Do not think of an answer.
points.text: A specific answer cannot be thought up. It can only be remembered.

points.head: Ask one question: which one?
points.text: Choose from six real things, each with a nickname.

points.head: Dig out the reasons at home.
points.text: Say why you did each thing, out loud, before the day.

how: Coloured boxes show example words. Grey is a weak answer, green is a strong one, blue is a line to say out loud. Boxes marked Try it now are short exercises.
Sam, who gives the full example answer, is made up. Square brackets mark things only you know.
